x: Awadh taluqdars, peasants and artisans joined the revolt in Awadh and western UP, while the big zamindars of Bengal stayed loyal.

s: Which of the following leaders is associated with a rising in the Andhra region during the Revolt of 1857?
x: Korukonda Subba Reddy led a rising in Andhra; Shah Mal (Baraut), Kunwar Singh (Bihar) and Khan Bahadur Khan (Bareilly) were in the north.

s: In which region of present Andhra Pradesh is Kadiri, where an attempt was made to incite rebellion in 1857?
x: Kadiri is a town of Rayalaseema; the 1857 attempt there was one of the sporadic Andhra risings.

s: What was the main cause of the failure of the revolt of 1857?
o: Lack of common strategy and central organization
Its effect was within a limited area
x: The revolt of the 1857 failed due to lack of common strategy and central leadership. This was one of the major reasons for the failure of the revolt of 1857. All the groups participated in this revolt for their own interests. There was no feeling of nationalism behind the mutiny and lack of clear vision.

s: The British were able to suppress the uprising of 1857 in Rajput state because:
o: The local Rajput rulers did not support revolutionaries
The educated middle class supported the British
The soldiers in cantonments were not prepared
The newspaper could not project the true aim of the
x: Expansion in limited areas, lack of unity and planning, no unified leadership and discipline, better resources of the British, role of traitors, the return of British troops from Crimea, least support of native rulers, non-cooperation from Sikhs and Punjabis as well as educated Indian middle class etc. were major causes behind the failure of the revolt of 1857.

s:
Consider the following statements about the failure of the Revolt of 1857:
1. The rebels lacked a common strategy and central organisation.
2. Major rulers of the Rajput states backed the British.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are causes of failure: no common strategy or central organisation, and big rulers such as the Rajput states sided with the British.
